notes.text: Turn 1, floor 1: Collapsed Stairwell, a hazard, was the first room. Gray alone reached Scramble 6 with Pick The Lock plus a Duck Under, clearing both thresholds and revealing a reward. Red held a full hand of four Charge In and a Shove the entire turn, no reason to spend Oomph cards Red had no use for, and the unspent-cards-stay-in-hand rule meant nothing was lost by sitting out. Felt right: a hazard room that only needs one stat gives one character a clean turn while the other watches, same shape as playtest 3 noted for Enemy rooms.

Floor 1 cleared in 2 turns (Gross Thing at Oomph 5, no Enemy-room-on-turn-1 luck this time but close). Ascend reward: gave Gray I Know Kung Fu, cost 3, Oomph 5, Holding draw-on-Scramble. This directly answers playtest 3's biggest finding (Gray has no route to Oomph). Picked it deliberately to see if one reward card changes Gray's shape. Settle your Stuff was a no-op this floor, no Stuff cards had entered either deck yet, so the step printed nothing to decide -- worth remembering for later floors once Stuff shows up.

Held I Know Kung Fu in hand instead of playing it, so its Holding draw-on-Scramble triggered twice while Gray played Duck Under and Pick The Lock. That is a real decision the Holding keyword creates: play the card for its stat now, or hold it for the passive and cash in the stat later. Eventually traded it away as payment to push Scramble from 4 to 8 for the second threshold anyway. This is the kind of choice playtest 3 never saw. Also: Ruptured Coolant Line gave both characters Bad Stuff on the lower threshold, and Gray now holds Panic, +2 Scramble to every room's thresholds while held, for the whole rest of the game unless it gets played or discarded. That is a persistent tax that stacks with the marathon model's growing decks -- worth watching whether it gets paid off or just sat on.

Spill Of Cargo paid out 3 Good Stuff on one clear: Coil Of Cable to Red, Pry Bar and Riot Shield to Gray. Riot Shield showed up on floor 2 turn 4 here too, same as playtest 3, and it is the same card: Scramble 3 for cost 1 that returns to hand whenever the room clears. If it clears every turn from here it is a free Scramble 3 forever. Watching whether it dominates the run the way playtest 3 said it did.

Clearing Collapsed Stairwell's Scramble 2 threshold Exhausts 1 from each deck, and the top of Red's deck happened to be Junk Launcher, the reward taken two floors back on floor 1. Under 0.2 Exhaust is permanent, so that card is gone for the rest of the run unless something un-exhausts it. A threshold whose outcome is Exhaust does not let you choose which card -- it is the top of the deck, so a good reward can vanish the same turn it might have been drawn. This is the marathon model's teeth: Exhaust is no longer a minor tempo cost, it is deck attrition that can eat your best cards at random.

cards.yaml has Torn Seal (bad_stuff, cost 2) with text: null. It has no printed rules text. Red just drew it into hand and the CLI shows it as [cost 2; Bad Stuff] with no effect line, no Holding, nothing. This looks like a design gap rather than a CLI bug: the card is incomplete in cards.yaml, so there is nothing wrong to fix in the engine, but flagging it since it will produce a card that does literally nothing if played or held.

Engine fidelity check: playing the second Overdrive (Exhaust 2) mid-Play with Red's deck down to 1 card triggered a discard-to-deck reshuffle inside the Exhaust resolution itself -- deck went 1 -> exhaust the 1 -> deck empty -> discard pile (5 cards) shuffled into a new deck -> exhaust 1 more from it. Ended at deck 4, discard 0, exhaust 6 (up from 4). This matches the rulebook's Empty deck rule (section 8: 'If you must draw or Exhaust a card and your deck is empty, first shuffle your discard pile to form a new deck') applying mid-Play phase, not just at Turn Start. Good sign for engine fidelity: the reshuffle is not special-cased to the draw step.

Engine fidelity / CLI: this Ascend at floor 2 -> 3 printed 487 numbered options for two players each with a 3-card reward offer and, between them, two Stuff cards to Settle (Red's Overcharged Battery, Gray's A Pair Of Stich-Em-Ups) plus several more Stuff cards the generator found buried in deck and discard (Coil Of Cable, Rust, Pry Bar, ...). Settle your Stuff (rulebook section 10.2) says 'search your deck and discard pile for Stuff cards' -- confirmed, the generator does search past the hand shown on screen, which is correct, but it crosses every found Stuff card's keep/shuffle choice, every scrap-target card option for each, and both characters' 3-way reward choice into one flat list. Went looking for 'Red takes Zen Mode; Gray takes In Step' with no Stuff kept and could not find it anywhere in the 487 lines -- spec.md names a 256-entry cap on the two characters' Ascend cross product as known debt, and this run hit a case beyond it where a specific legal combination was simply absent from the list, not just hard to find. Chose 'Red takes Zen Mode; Gray declines' instead of the Gray reward I wanted, because I could not locate the combination that had both.

Tuning-independent shape, floors 2-3: Settle your Stuff has read as pure bookkeeping every time so far, not a decision. The default (shuffle into the pool) is almost always correct because a kept Stuff card costs a permanent non-Stuff card from deck or discard, and nothing so far has been worth that price -- the Stuff cards offered (Overcharged Battery, Torn Seal, A Pair Of Stich-Em-Ups) are not strong enough to pay a real card for. Combined with the missing-combination problem in note above, the practical move has been 'decline everything, keep nothing' every single Ascend so far. Whether that is a tuning problem (nothing worth keeping) or a structural one (keeping is never worth a card) is a question for the designer once cards are re-tuned.

Engine fidelity / rulebook gap, worth flagging clearly: Turn Start this turn, Gray's hand size before the draw was 1 (Crowbar). Draw up to five (rulebook, Each Turn 1.2) should draw exactly 4 cards for Gray. The log shows Gray drew 7: Duck Under, Peek Around Corner, Pick The Lock, [deck empty, reshuffle], Pick The Lock, Catch Your Breath, Duck Under, I Know Kung Fu -- landing Gray at hand size 8, three over the stated cap. Red drew exactly 3 cards this turn (hand 2 -> 5, correct), and the 3rd card Red drew was My Head Is Quantum Spinning, cards.yaml text 'Holding: whenever you draw a card, your partner must also draw a card.' Three extra Gray draws exactly matches Red's three draws this turn, so the effect looks like it fired for all of Red's draws this Turn Start even though MHQS only entered Red's hand as the LAST of those three draws -- it could not have been 'in hand' (the Holding keyword's stated trigger condition) for the first two. Either the engine batches Holding draw-triggers over the whole Turn Start step rather than checking hand membership in real time, or there is a genuine ordering bug. Separately: the rulebook's 'draw up to five' doesn't say whether a Holding-triggered forced draw is capped at 5 or can push a hand past it -- worth a question to the designer either way, since MHQS pushing a hand to 8 is a big stamina hit for a card that isn't in that hand at all.

Stopping at the turn-25 limit, floor 5 of 10, mid-turn-start. Neither character came close to Down: Red is on deck 9 + discard 1 + exhaust 11 (of an original 12-card deck, so exhaust alone now exceeds the starting deck size), Gray is deck 2 + discard 6 + exhaust 7. Stamina pressure exists but is slow -- both decks kept cycling through discard recycling and neither hand was ever empty at a moment it mattered. The permanent Exhaust pile is the standout number: Red has exhausted 11 cards total across five floors, several of them good reward cards (Junk Launcher, Fast Follow, Second Wind, Reckless Swing all got eaten by threshold-Exhaust or Overdrive's Exhaust 2 at some point in this run) rather than starter filler. Under 0.1 rules exhaust was recoverable at Ascend; under 0.2 it just accumulates. That is the biggest structural difference this run surfaced, tuning aside.

CLI: bin/nvu replay runs/4.json --quiet printed the full final table (floor, both hands, everything) before the one-line verdict, same as playtest 3 note 9 flagged for this rules version's engine. Spec.md says --quiet prints only the verdict. Still open.

Rulebook gap: the Play phase section says 'You may not draw during this phase,' but I Know Kung Fu's Holding text is 'when you play a card with Scramble, draw 1 card,' and this triggered repeatedly during Play all through this run (e.g. logs around turn 3, 7, 12, 19). The engine allows it every time, uncapped, with no error. Read narrowly, the rulebook's ban on drawing in Play and this card's printed effect contradict each other. Read generously, 'you may not draw' means the player cannot choose to draw as an action, and a card-triggered draw is a different thing. The engine has clearly taken the generous reading. Worth a flat question to the designer: is a Play-phase forced draw from a card effect meant to be exempt from the 'no draiw during this phase' line, and if so should the rulebook say so explicitly, since as printed it reads like a flat ban.

Rulebook gap: Stuff gained on the turn a floor Ascends. This run never happened to draw Good/Bad Stuff and Ascend in the same turn, so it went untested, but nothing in section 10 (Ascending) says what happens if a Stuff card is still in the play zone or was just gained when Cleanup and the Ascend steps run. Section 10 step 1 is 'Shuffle your hand into your deck' -- a Stuff card gained into hand that turn would just go in with everything else, which seems fine, but a Stuff card returned to hand at end of turn (Riot Shield's own text) landing mid-Ascend was never exercised this run. Flagging as an untested edge rather than a confirmed problem.

Re-tune input, not a verdict: Zen Mode (cost 0, Holding: you don't Exhaust) combined with Reckless-style Oomph-for-Exhaust cards is a strong synergy under 0.2 specifically because Exhaust is now permanent -- it converts a card that used to cost real deck attrition into a pure stat card with zero downside for as long as Zen Mode stays in hand. It stopped an Exhaust twice this run (floor 3 and floor 5) with the line 'Zen Mode stops it,' which read clearly both times. Whether that is too strong is a balance question for after re-tuning, but the interaction itself is worth recording since it is a direct product of the 0.1 -> 0.2 change to Exhaust.
